props.description: Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the input when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys. The first item can then be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> again from the input, or the last item can be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> from the input. The input is always included in the focus loop per [ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/). When disabled, focus does not move when on the last element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd>, or when on the first element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd>.

props.description: The items to be displayed in the list. props.description: Filtered items to display in the list. When provided, the list uses these items instead of filtering the `items` prop internally. When `items` is also provided, this array must preserve its flat or grouped structure. With a `createItems()` collection, pass source items rather than derived values. Nullish entries are not supported, as in `items`. Use when you want to control filtering logic externally with the `useFilter()` hook.
props.name: filteredItems

props.name: limit

With a `createItems()` collection, this receives the derived value, and the collection's `getLabel` takes precedence for values it can resolve.

props.description: When the item values are objects (`<Combobox.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for form submission. props.description: Callback fired when an item is highlighted or unhighlighted. components.use: For every form control that has a label, a description or an error: it lays them out and marks the field invalid. A control that needs only a name takes a Label or an `aria-label`.
components.example:
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, FieldLegend, FieldSet, Input } from "@basis/ui";

<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Ticket</FieldLegend>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="cusip">CUSIP</FieldLabel>
      <Input id="cusip" aria-describedby="cusip-help" />
      <FieldDescription id="cusip-help">Nine characters, check digit last.</FieldDescription>
    </Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>;

import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  Button,
} from "@basis/ui";

<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>Cancel order</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Cancel this order?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>The order leaves the book and cannot be restored.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Keep it</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction>Cancel order</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;

components.example:
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@basis/ui";

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit position</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Edit position</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Change the book this position sits in.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DialogClose>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>;

</Popover>;

import { Button, Sheet, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

import { Bps, Money, Num, Pct, Price32 } from "@basis/ui";

components.name: UserMenu

components.use: AppShell puts one in its sidebar's footer; use it alone only in a layout of the app's own, under BasisApp.
components.example:
import { UserMenu } from "@basis/ui";

<UserMenu />;

Its fields read text, as a CSV's cells are and a workbook's are given (a number as Excel shows it, a date as ISO 8601, a boolean as TRUE or FALSE), such as `z.coerce.number()`, `amountSchema(parSuffixes)` or `z.enum([...])`; an empty cell is a missing value, which an optional field takes.
props.name: schema

props.description: The header, or headers, a key's column goes by in a file, when not the key itself; the first heads the preview.
props.name: headers

props.description: Receives the valid rows, typed by the schema, when the user confirms. While a promise it returns is pending the button waits; if it rejects, its error shows and the preview stays.
props.name: onImport

props.description: The largest file it reads, in bytes; 5 MB unless set.
props.name: maxBytes

props.description: The most rows a file may hold under its header; 10,000 unless set.
props.name: maxRows

props.description: The drop zone's title; "Drop a CSV or Excel file here" unless set.
props.name: title

props.description: The workbook's sheet to import, by name, ignoring case; unless set, the first visible sheet that holds the schema's columns, and the user may choose another that does. A CSV has no sheets.
props.name: sheet

components.purpose: A CSV or Excel import, checked against `schema`, that hands the app the valid rows once the user confirms.
components.use: For rows the user has in a CSV file or an Excel workbook, checked against a schema before the app takes them. To read a file in code, use parseCsv or readWorkbook from `@basis/ui/utils`.

components.name: FilterBar

props.description: The page's filters and their values, as `useFilters` returns them.
props.name: filters

props.description: The name of the bar's search landmark; "Filters" unless set.
props.name: label

props.description: What sits at the end of the controls, such as the page's saved views.
props.name: actions

props.description: Classes that place it: margin, width, and flex or grid placement. Its look comes from its props, never from classes.
props.name: className

components.purpose: A bar of the page's filters, kept in its address's search parameters, with a chip for each active filter.
components.use: For filtering a page's table, grid or list by its fields: text, a choice, several choices, a range of days or a range of numbers. Define the filters with `defineFilters`, give the route `filterSearchSchema(filters)` as its `validateSearch`, and give the bar `useFilters(filters)`; filter the rows with `filterRows`, or send `values` to the API. For a search box over one DataTable, DataTable's own filter is enough.

components.name: FormDateField

components.name: FormCheckboxField

props.description: The field's label.

components.purpose: A flag, ticked or not, its label beside the box.

components.name: FormSelectField

props.description: The field's label.

props.description: A line under the control that says what to enter, such as "Twelve capital letters and digits".
props.name: description

props.description: The control's id; one made from the field's name unless set.

props.description: The TanStack Form field, `form.Field`'s render argument.
props.name: field

props.description: The options, each its value and the words it shows.
props.name: options

components.purpose: A choice of a few options, on the browser's own select, such as an enum a generated schema declares. A field that starts with no choice holds `""`, which the placeholder stands for until an option is chosen.
components.use: For a choice among a handful of options in a form on TanStack Form. For a long list, use Combobox.

components.name: UnsavedChangesGuard

props.description: Whether the page holds changes not yet saved, such as TanStack Form's `form.state.isDirty` until it submits.
props.name: when

props.description: The dialog's title; "Leave without saving?" unless set.

props.name: description

components.name: TypedConfirmDialog

props.description: Whether the dialog is open; the page holds it, as the action's button opens it.
props.name: open

props.description: Called to open or close it: Cancel, Escape and a confirmed action close it.

props.description: What is asked, such as "Delete the book Rates?".
props.name: title

props.name: actionLabel

props.name: onConfirm

components.purpose: A dialog that asks for a name to be typed before an action that cannot be undone.

components.name: SavedViews

props.description: Where the views live: `browserViewStore` for this browser alone, or `apiViewStore` over the app's API.

props.description: The page's state now, which a view saves.

components.purpose: A menu of a page's saved views: apply one, save the page's state as a new one, or save changes to, rename, make the default or delete the one shown. Give it the store, the page's state and `onApply`, which puts a view's state on the page; the default view is applied once the views load, unless `applyDefault` is false.
components.use: For views a user saves of a grid's, a pivot's or a chart's layout, or of a table's sort and filters.

components.name: CellBar

props.description: The value the bar stands for.
props.name: value

props.description: The cell's text, over the bar, such as the value through `Num` or `Money`.
props.name: children

components.purpose: A table cell's text over a bar of its value.

components.name: QueryState

props.description: The query, such as a generated client's `usePositions()`.

props.description: What the idle state says, while a disabled query waits for what it needs, such as "Choose a book", and what will show once it has it.

props.description: The idle state's line under its title, such as what will show once the query has what it needs.
props.name: idleDescription

props.description: What stands in while the data first loads; three lines of skeleton by default.

props.name: className

components.purpose: A query's data, or what stands in for it: loading, failed, empty, and how old it is.
components.use: For every state of a query's data in one place: loading, waiting, failed, empty and stale. For an error alone, use ErrorAlert; a DataTable takes its query's `loading` and `error` itself.

components.name: Sparkline

props.description: The values in order, such as each day's close; null or NaN where one is missing.

components.purpose: A small line of `values`, 96 by 24 pixels unless className sizes it, such as `h-8 w-full`.

components.name: StatCard

components.name: ErrorAlert

props.description: The error to show, such as a query's or a mutation's `error`; with `null` or `undefined` nothing renders.

props.description: Adds a "Try again" button that calls it, such as a query's `refetch`.

components.purpose: A destructive Alert describing `error`, announced at once to a screen reader and named by its title.

components.example:
import { ErrorAlert } from "@basis/ui";

<ErrorAlert error={new Error("The positions could not be loaded.")} onRetry={() => undefined} />;

components.name: BasisApp

props.description: The app's TanStack Router, made with `createRouter({ routeTree })`. Its routes render once the user is known. Unless it sets its own, BasisApp gives it an error component, a not-found component and an `onCatch` that reports to telemetry.
props.name: router

props.description: The sign-in adapter: the firm's, `anonymousSignIn()` for an app with no sign-in, or `fakeSignIn()` in tests and development.
props.name: signIn

props.description: Where errors, events and timings go; the console by default.
props.name: telemetry

props.description: The query client, for a test that reads its cache; one from `createQueryClient()` by default.
props.name: queryClient

props.description: The mode, density, motion and theme to show in place of the stored choice, which it otherwise follows: for a page told them another way, as the gallery is by its query. A choice made in the user menu is still stored, and shown at once.
props.name: preferences

props.description: The parent domain the firm's apps share, such as `apps.example.com`, for the cookie that holds the user's mode, density, motion and theme, so that a choice made in one app is every app's, and a page left open follows it. On a host that is neither the domain nor under it, such as `localhost` in development, the choice is this app's alone, as it is without this.
props.name: preferencesDomain

components.purpose: The app's providers: telemetry, the query client, the toasts, an error boundary round everything, the signed-in session, and the router. It also keeps the page in the user's mode, density, motion and theme as they change them, in this app or another on the `preferencesDomain` it is given, or in the `preferences` it is given, signs the user out when the API says their session has ended, and asks them to sign in when it says a request needs them to.
components.use: For an app's entry point: render it once at the root, with the router and the sign-in adapter. A test renders the app at an address with renderApp from `@basis/ui/testing`.

components.name: ParallaxProvider

props.description: Where the engine's worker comes from. Leave it out: the package starts its own worker, which an app's bundler finds beside the package's code. A test or a page that serves the worker itself passes a function that starts one, or the URL that serves `@basis/parallax/worker`. Define it outside the component, or let the React Compiler keep it: a different worker starts a new engine, without the data.
props.name: worker

props.description: Starts the worker when the provider mounts, rather than when the first data loads, so that the first rows show sooner. Every page under the provider then downloads the engine, about 1 MB compressed, whether or not it shows parallax. Off by default.
props.name: prewarm

props.description: The theme parallax draws in: `basisTheme`, `@basis/ui`'s own, by default.
props.name: theme

props.description: The scheme it draws in: by default the page's mode, as `@basis/ui`'s preferences set it; `auto` follows the system's.
props.name: scheme

props.description: The part of the app that shows parallax: every grid, pivot and chart inside it uses the one engine.
props.name: children

components.purpose: Starts parallax's engine for the tree inside it, in a Web Worker, and ends it, freeing its memory, when it unmounts. It installs the theme's stylesheets, and follows the page's mode and density, so that every grid, pivot and chart inside repaints when they change.
components.use: Once, around the part of the app that shows a Grid, a Pivot or a Chart, since it starts the engine's worker. Put it around only the pages that use parallax: with `prewarm`, every page under it downloads the engine.

props.description: The dataset to show, from `useDataset`.

props.description: The view: grouping, sorting, filters, formats and widths. The dataset is `dataset`'s. Left out, the grid shows every column in the table's order, each by its API's display format. A dataset of rows of a known type, `useDataset<Position>`, takes only its columns' names.

Without it, the bar shows the time the source was read and how long ago, when `useDataset`'s `sourceAsOfMicros` gives one, and no "as of" otherwise: never the time the browser loaded the table. A string that is not a calendar date shows an `ERROR` line there, with the fix, in place of the date.

components.name: Pivot

props.description: The dataset to pivot, from `useDataset`.

functions.name: useComboboxAnchor
functions.purpose: A ref for ComboboxChips, passed to ComboboxContent as `anchor` so the popup lines up with the chips.

functions.name: useSidebar
functions.purpose: The sidebar's state and its setters, inside a SidebarProvider.

functions.name: createToastManager
functions.purpose: Base UI's own: `createToastManager()` makes a manager apart from the app's, for a `<Toaster toastManager={...}>` of its own, as in a test, and `useToastManager()` reads the toasts and the same methods inside a provider.

functions.name: toast
functions.purpose: The app's toasts: `toast.add({ title, description, type })` raises one and returns its id, which `toast.update` and `toast.close` take; `toast.promise` shows one for a promise, loading until it settles. `type` picks the look: `success`, `warning`, `info` or `destructive` (or `error`, which `toast.promise` sets on a rejection), each with its icon; `loading`, with a spinner; anything else, or none, is the plain toast. A toast closes itself after five seconds unless `timeout` says otherwise, and `0` keeps it until it is closed. `priority: "high"` announces it at once, for what the user must act on now.

functions.name: useToastManager
functions.purpose: Base UI's own: `createToastManager()` makes a manager apart from the app's, for a `<Toaster toastManager={...}>` of its own, as in a test, and `useToastManager()` reads the toasts and the same methods inside a provider.

functions.name: amountSchema
functions.purpose: Takes what an AmountInput holds and gives the number. It accepts the number the input read, and rejects the text the input holds while what was typed reads as no number, with the parser's reason, such as `"k" is not a suffix this field accepts: use m, mm, bn.` `null`, an empty field, fails with "Enter an amount."; add `.nullable()` for a field that may stay empty. Its input type takes `null`, as a form's values do while the field is empty.
functions.signature: amountSchema(suffixes: Suffixes = amountSuffixes): z.ZodType<number, number | string | null>

functions.name: dateRangePresets
functions.purpose: Every preset, in the order a picker lists them.

functions.name: rangeForPreset
functions.purpose: A preset's range as of a date, on a calendar, SIFMA's unless set. To date runs from the period's first business day to the last business day on or before `asOf`; a prior period from its first business day to its last; a trailing one from the first business day on or after the same date its months before, to the last business day on or before `asOf`.
functions.signature: rangeForPreset(preset: DateRangePreset, asOf: Temporal.PlainDate, calendar: Calendar = sifma): DateRange

functions.name: defaultAsOfDate
functions.purpose: The as-of date a field starts at: the last business day before today, the last close whose data is complete.
functions.signature: defaultAsOfDate({ calendar = sifma, today }: AsOfOptions = {}): Temporal.PlainDate

functions.name: useRouteEntries
functions.purpose: The app's pages, in the order its route tree declares them.

functions.name: useShortcut
functions.purpose: Declares a keyboard shortcut while the component is shown: `useShortcut("mod+k", "Open the command palette", open)`. Inside a `ShortcutProvider`, which `AppShell` holds; it does nothing outside one. Inside a `ShortcutScope`, such as the one AppShell holds round the page shown, it belongs to that scope, and wins over a shortcut outside it that takes the same keys, so a page's shortcuts are its own.
functions.signature: useShortcut(keys: string, description: string, run: () => void): void

functions.name: displayFormatMetadata
functions.purpose: The Arrow field metadata key that holds a column's display format.

functions.name: displayFormatSchema
functions.purpose: How a number is shown, by kind: a plain number, money in a currency, a fraction as a percentage or in basis points, a price, or a Treasury price in 32nds to its finest step.
functions.signature: const displayFormatSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [ z.object({ decimals, kind: z.literal("number") }), z.object({ curren…

functions.name: readDisplayFormat
functions.purpose: The display format `declared` holds: an object, or the JSON text Arrow metadata holds. `undefined` for anything else, a kind this version does not know included, so the value shows by the formatter's defaults.

functions.name: numberText
functions.purpose: A number as text, for a string such as a toast's or an accessible name, by the same rule `Num` shows it with: `numberText(150000, { decimals: 0 })` is `150,000`.

functions.name: apiViewStore
functions.purpose: A store over the app's API, which keeps a user's views wherever they sign in. A call that fails rejects the operation with its error, which `BasisApp` shows as a toast, as it does for every failed mutation.
functions.signature: apiViewStore<TState>({ key, calls, parse, }: ApiViewStoreOptions<TState>): SavedViewStore<TState>

functions.name: browserViewStore
functions.purpose: A store in the browser's storage: the user's views on this browser, which no other user or machine sees. A storage that refuses a write, as a full one does, rejects the operation with its error.
functions.signature: browserViewStore<TState>({ key, parse, storage = globalThis.localStorage, }: BrowserViewStoreOptions<TState>): SavedViewStore<TState>

functions.name: defineFilters
functions.purpose: A page's filters, checked, with each choice's options kept as the literal values the page wrote, so the route's search parameters and `FilterValues` take only those. Define them once, outside any component, and give them to `filterSearchSchema` for the route and to `useFilters` for the page.
functions.signature: defineFilters<const TFilters extends FilterDefinitions>(filters: TFilters): TFilters
functions.use: For the filters of a page's table, grid or list, kept in the address. Throws one ERROR line for a choice with no options, an empty option or one listed twice.

functions.name: filterRows
functions.purpose: The rows every active filter keeps, in their order. A row's field passes text that it holds, ignoring case; the option chosen, or any of those chosen; or a date or number inside the range. With no filter active it returns `rows` itself.
functions.signature: filterRows<TRow, TFilters extends FilterDefinitions>(rows: readonly TRow[], { filters, values, fields }: FilterRowsOptions<TRow, TFilters>): readonly TRow[]
functions.use: For a page's own filtering of rows it holds, such as a Table's or a DataTable's data under a FilterBar. Rows an API filters are filtered there: send it the values instead.

functions.name: filterSearchSchema
functions.purpose: The Zod schema of the filters as search parameters, for the route's `validateSearch`, so the router types them. Each parameter is optional, and a value the filter cannot take is read as absent. Extend it with the route's other parameters: `filterSearchSchema(tradeFilters).extend({ selected: z.string().optional() })`. Throws one ERROR line for filters `defineFilters` would refuse.
functions.signature: filterSearchSchema<const TFilters extends FilterDefinitions>(filters: TFilters): FilterSearchSchema<TFilters>
functions.use: For the route of a page with a FilterBar, as its `validateSearch`. Its output type is the page's `FilterValues`.

functions.name: useFilters
functions.purpose: The page's filters, read from its address's search parameters and written back to them. Its route's `validateSearch` is `filterSearchSchema(filters)`, with the same filters. Give the result to `FilterBar`, and its `values` to `filterRows` or a query.
functions.signature: useFilters<const TFilters extends FilterDefinitions>(filters: TFilters): FilterState<TFilters>
functions.use: For a page with a FilterBar: call it once, then pass it to the bar and read `values` for the rows. Back and Forward restore the filters, and a link to the page opens them.

functions.name: FormatError
functions.purpose: A format that cannot be used.

functions.name: createFormatter
functions.purpose: Checks a format and returns its formatter. Throws `FormatError` for an unknown zone, more than 30 decimals, or a percentage that also abbreviates.

functions.name: defaultZone
functions.purpose: The display zone when a format names none.

functions.name: maxDecimals
functions.purpose: The most decimals a format may show, Excel's limit.

functions.name: nullText
functions.purpose: Text for a null value.

functions.name: outOfRangeText
functions.purpose: Text for a value outside the range a date can show.

functions.name: undefinedText
functions.purpose: Text for an undefined result, such as NaN or a percentage of zero.

functions.name: amountSuffixes
functions.purpose: Amounts: `k` thousands, `m` and `mm` millions, `b` and `bn` billions.

functions.name: parSuffixes
functions.purpose: Amounts in bond-market style, where `m` means thousands and `mm` millions.

functions.name: parseAmount
functions.purpose: Reads `text` into the number it means, such as 1500000 for `1.5mm` or 0.0025 for `25bp`, or says why it cannot: the text is read exactly, then converted to the nearest double.
functions.signature: parseAmount(text: string, suffixes: Suffixes = amountSuffixes): ParseResult

functions.name: rateSuffixes
functions.purpose: Rates: `%` hundredths and `bp` or `bps` basis points, ten-thousandths.

functions.name: applyPreferences
functions.purpose: Puts the preferences on the page's root element: the `dark` class, `color-scheme`, `data-density`, `data-motion` and `data-theme`. `data-density` and `data-theme` always name the density and the theme, so that whatever reads them, such as parallax's canvases, need not know the stylesheet's base; the default theme's rules sit at `:root` and hold whatever `data-theme` says, and every other theme's under its `[data-theme="NAME"]`. A change to any of them holds every transition off until it is drawn, so the page changes in one frame, as its canvases do, where some sixty controls' colours would otherwise cross-fade and a density change lay the page out frame by frame, and then dispatches `themeChangeEvent` on the root element.
functions.signature: applyPreferences(root: PreferencesRoot, preferences: Preferences, systemDark: boolean): void

functions.name: defaultPreferences
functions.purpose: Compact is the default density, the maintainer's choice on 2026-11-07. The stylesheet's base is compact too, and `data-density="comfortable"` widens it, so a page shows the default before the head script or `followPreferences` has run, and without either, as in a test.

functions.name: followPreferences
functions.purpose: Applies the stored preferences now, and again whenever the cookie or the operating system's mode changes, the cookie changed by this app or by another on the shared domain. Given `options.domain`, it first moves a choice this app kept for itself onto the shared domain. Given `shown`, it applies those in place of the stored ones and follows only the operating system's mode, which a `system` mode reads: for a page told its preferences another way, as the gallery is by its query. Returns a function that stops following them.

functions.name: headScript
functions.purpose: A script for the page's `<head>` that applies the stored preferences before the first paint, so the page never flashes the wrong mode. It repeats `parsePreferences` and `applyPreferences` in plain JavaScript; a test holds the two to the same answers.
functions.signature: const headScript = `(() => { try { const themes = ${JSON.stringify(themeNames)}; const match = /(?:^|;\\s*)${preferenc…

functions.name: parsePreferences
functions.purpose: Reads the preferences from a `document.cookie` string. Anything missing or unknown falls back to the default.

functions.name: preferencesCookie
functions.purpose: The cookie's name. Its value is the mode, the density, the motion and the theme joined by dots, such as `dark.compact.full.default`. A value written before the motion or the theme was reads them as the default's, and so does a theme no longer shipped, since a user's cookie can outlive a theme.

functions.name: readPreferences
functions.purpose: The preferences stored in this page's cookies.

functions.name: resolveMode
functions.purpose: The mode a page shows, given the preference and whether the operating system is in dark mode.

functions.name: serializePreferences
functions.purpose: The `document.cookie` assignment that stores the preferences for a year.

functions.name: themeChangeEvent
functions.purpose: The event `applyPreferences` dispatches on the root element, bubbling to the document, once it has changed the mode, density, motion or theme shown: whatever draws from the theme's tokens outside CSS, such as parallax's canvases, reads them again. Code that changes the tokens in a way no attribute shows, such as by swapping a stylesheet, dispatches it on the document.

functions.name: writePreferences
functions.purpose: Stores the preferences, on the shared domain when `options` names one and the page is on it, and applies them to this page at once. Other pages follow through `followPreferences`.

functions.name: themeNames
functions.purpose: Every shipped theme's name, the default first.

functions.name: tokenNames
functions.purpose: Every token's name, the same in every theme, for code that reads tokens at run time, such as parallax's canvases.

functions.name: ApiError
functions.purpose: What a failed call throws, so TanStack Query's `error` holds the parsed problem details.

functions.name: apiFetch
functions.purpose: The mutator orval's generated client calls for every operation.

functions.name: apiPrefix
functions.purpose: The ingress routes `/api` to the API and the rest to the UI, so the browser makes no cross-origin calls.

functions.name: arrowStream
functions.purpose: The media type basis's contract returns datasets in.

functions.name: isApiError
functions.purpose: Whether `error` is the `ApiError` a generated hook fails with, holding the API's status and problem details.

functions.name: setTokenSource
functions.purpose: Sets where `apiFetch` gets the user's token. The app shell calls it once, at startup.

functions.name: errorsOnFields
functions.purpose: A 422's errors by the field each names, or `undefined` when the form's fields cannot hold the failure: any failure but a 422, a 422 that names no field, and one that names a field the form does not have.
functions.signature: errorsOnFields(error: unknown, fields: ReadonlySet<string> | readonly string[]): Record<string, readonly string[]> | undefined

functions.name: submitErrors
functions.purpose: What a failed submit leaves on the form: the errors of the fields a 422 names, or `message`, a form error, for a failure they cannot hold, which the page shows with ErrorAlert.
functions.signature: submitErrors(error: unknown, { fields, message, }: { readonly fields: ReadonlySet<string> | readonly string[]; readonly message: string }): SubmitErrors

functions.name: fieldErrorSchema
functions.purpose: One field's error in a 422: a request-body field named by a JSON Pointer, or a query or path parameter by name.
functions.signature: const fieldErrorSchema = z.union([ z.object({ detail: z.string(), pointer: z.string() }), z.object({ detail: z.string(), par…

functions.name: fieldErrors
functions.purpose: A 422's errors keyed by the form field each names, in TanStack Form's naming, such as `legs[0].price`; errors for the whole body sit under `""`, and parameters under their names.
functions.signature: fieldErrors(problem: Problem | ValidationProblem): ReadonlyMap<string, readonly string[]>

functions.name: fieldName
functions.purpose: A JSON Pointer's path as TanStack Form names the field: `["legs", 0, "price"]` → `legs[0].price`.

functions.name: pointerPath
functions.purpose: The path a JSON Pointer in URI-fragment form names, such as `#/legs/0/price` → `["legs", 0, "price"]`. `#` alone names the whole body, an empty path. Returns `undefined` for text that is not a fragment pointer.

functions.name: problemSchema
functions.purpose: Problem details. Every member is optional in RFC 9457; `type` defaults to `about:blank`. basis's document declares `detail` and `instance` as a string or `null`. Unknown members are kept, since a problem type may add its own, as basis's `data` does.
functions.signature: const problemSchema = z.looseObject({ detail: z.string().nullish(), instance: z.string().nullish(), status: z.number().in…

functions.name: validationProblemSchema
functions.purpose: A 422's problem details, naming each field at fault.

functions.name: describeError
functions.purpose: The words for `error`: problem details when the API answered them, otherwise the kind of failure.

functions.name: createQueryClient
functions.purpose: A QueryClient with basis-ui's defaults: queries stay fresh for 30 seconds, and retry twice, but only after a network failure or a 502, 503 or 504. A mutation retries twice only after a `keys-unavailable` 503. `BasisApp` makes one; a test may make its own.

functions.name: useSession
functions.purpose: The signed-in session: `const { user, signIn, signOut } = useSession();`. Only components inside `BasisApp` have one.

functions.name: toastError
functions.purpose: Raises a toast for `error`, such as a failed save, and returns its id: the problem's title, then its detail, each field a 422 names and the request's reference, a line each. `BasisApp` raises one for every failed mutation unless the mutation's `meta` says `{ errorToast: false }`. The toast stays until the user closes it, and a screen reader announces it at once. The same error, its title, detail and fields alike, raised again within 10 seconds of the last while its toast is open, raises no new toast: that one shows the latest reference and how many times it happened, and its id is returned. Once the toast is closed, the error raises a new one.

functions.name: anonymousSignIn
functions.purpose: The sign-in adapter of an app with no sign-in system: every user is anonymous, requests carry no token, and the shell offers no sign-in. `<BasisApp signIn={anonymousSignIn()} />`.

functions.name: fakeSignIn
functions.purpose: A sign-in adapter for tests and development: `user` is signed in at once, and each token is a JWT for them, signed with basis's development key, with their `name` and `email` as claims. A basis API on a developer's desktop whose settings verify with the development key, such as `basis dev`'s, accepts it; any other refuses it with a 401. `signOut` makes the user anonymous, and `signIn` signs them in again at once.
functions.signature: fakeSignIn({ user = fakeUser, issuer = developmentKeyId, audience = developmentKeyId, claims = {}, }: FakeSignInOptions = {}): SignIn

functions.name: fakeUser
functions.purpose: The user `fakeSignIn` signs in when it is given none.

functions.name: consoleTelemetry
functions.purpose: The telemetry `BasisApp` reports to unless given another: each error, event and timing written to the console.

functions.name: useTelemetry
functions.purpose: The app's telemetry, as `BasisApp` was given it: `useTelemetry().event("position.created", { book })`.

functions.name: defaultRounding
functions.purpose: Excel's rounding, which a number in a card must match.

functions.name: sumPrecise
functions.purpose: The exact sum of doubles, rounded once, where adding them in turn would round at every step: `[0.1, 0.2, 0.3]` sums to 0.6, not 0.6000000000000001, and `[1e100, 1, -1e100]` to 1, not 0. NaN in, or both infinities, gives NaN.

functions.name: roundToTick
functions.purpose: The multiple of `tick` nearest `value` by `rounding`, read at each double's shortest digits: `roundToTick(4.1337, 0.005)` is 4.135. Throws `RangeError` unless the tick is positive and both are finite.
functions.signature: roundToTick(value: number, tick: number, rounding: Rounding = defaultRounding): number

functions.name: formatThirtySeconds
functions.purpose: Writes a price in 32nds: `99-16`, `99-16+`, `99-162`, and `-0-04+` for a negative change. The price is read at 8 decimals, then rounded to the precision's step, so `formatThirtySeconds(price, { precision: "halves" })` shows only `99-16` or `99-16+`.

functions.name: parseThirtySeconds
functions.purpose: Reads a price typed in 32nds, `99-16`, `99-16+`, `99-162` or `99-164` (the same as `99-16+`), or a whole number of points such as `100`, into its value: `99-16+` is 99.515625, which a double holds exactly.

functions.name: delta
functions.purpose: `to - from`.

functions.name: percentChange
functions.purpose: The change from `from` to `to` as a fraction of `from`'s size, `(to - from) / |from|`: 0.05 for a rise from 100 to 105. Dividing by the size keeps the sign with the direction of the move, so a loss that narrows from -100 to -50 is +0.5, where Excel's `(to - from) / from` gives -0.5. Show it with `Pct`.

functions.name: shares
functions.purpose: Each value's weight in the total, as a fraction to `scale` decimals, the weights summing to exactly 1 at that scale. Each value is read at its shortest digits; every weight is its exact share rounded down or up by one unit in the last digit, and the units still short of 1 go to the largest remainders, the earlier value first on a tie: the largest remainder method. Negative values, as in a long and short book, take negative weights.
functions.signature: shares(values: readonly number[], { scale }: { readonly scale: number }): Shares

functions.name: chunk
functions.purpose: The items in runs of `size`, the last run holding what is left. Throws `RangeError` unless `size` is a positive integer.
functions.signature: chunk<TItem>(items: readonly TItem[], size: number): TItem[][]

functions.name: countBy
functions.purpose: How many items give each key. Keys no item gives are absent, not zero.
functions.signature: countBy<TItem, TKey extends PropertyKey>(items: readonly TItem[], mapper: Visit<TItem, TKey>): Partial<Record<TKey, number>>

functions.name: keyBy
functions.purpose: An object of the items by the key each one gives; a later item with the same key replaces an earlier one. Keys no item gives are absent, so each value may be `undefined`.
functions.signature: keyBy<TItem, TKey extends PropertyKey>(items: readonly TItem[], getKeyFromItem: Visit<TItem, TKey>): Partial<Record<TKey, TItem>>

functions.name: maxBy
functions.purpose: The item with the largest value, the first on a tie; `undefined` only for no items.
functions.signature: maxBy<TItem>(items: readonly [TItem, ...TItem[]], getValue: Visit<TItem, number>): TItem

functions.name: minBy
functions.purpose: The item with the smallest value, the first on a tie; `undefined` only for no items.
functions.signature: minBy<TItem>(items: readonly [TItem, ...TItem[]], getValue: Visit<TItem, number>): TItem

functions.name: partition
functions.purpose: The items that pass, then the items that fail, each in order. A type guard narrows both halves.
functions.signature: partition<TItem, TPassed extends TItem>(items: readonly TItem[], isInTruthy: (item: TItem, index: number, items: readonly TItem[]) => item is TPassed): [truthy: TPassed[], falsy: Exclude<TItem, TPassed>[]]

functions.name: range
functions.purpose: The numbers from `start` up to, not including, `end`, by `step`; with one argument, from 0 up to it: `range(4)` is `[0, 1, 2, 3]` and `range(0, -6, -2)` is `[0, -2, -4]`. Throws `RangeError` unless `step` is a nonzero integer.
functions.signature: range(startOrEnd: number, end?: number, step = 1): number[]

functions.name: uniqBy
functions.purpose: The first item for each distinct value `mapper` gives, compared as a `Set` compares, in order.
functions.signature: uniqBy<TItem, TValue>(items: readonly TItem[], mapper: Visit<TItem, TValue>): TItem[]

functions.name: zip
functions.purpose: Rows of the arrays' items, one row per index of the longest array. A shorter array gives `undefined` past its end, as lodash's `zip` does, and the types say so.

functions.name: entries
functions.purpose: The object's own enumerable string-keyed entries, typed by its keys and values.

functions.name: fromEntries
functions.purpose: An object of the entries. Keys the entries do not cover are absent, so each value may be `undefined`. A key such as `__proto__` is kept as data.
functions.signature: fromEntries<TKey extends PropertyKey, TValue>(pairs: Iterable<readonly [TKey, TValue]>): Partial<Record<TKey, TValue>>

functions.name: keys
functions.purpose: The object's own enumerable string keys, typed as its keys.
functions.signature: keys<TObject extends object>(value: TObject): (keyof TObject & string)[]

functions.name: mapValues
functions.purpose: A new object with the same keys, each value replaced by what `getNewValue` returns for it.
functions.signature: mapValues<TObject extends object, TValue>(value: TObject, getNewValue: ( current: TObject[keyof TObject & string], key: keyof TObject & string, object: TObject, ) => TValue): Record<keyof TObject & string, TValue>

functions.name: omit
functions.purpose: A new object with every own enumerable string key but the listed ones.
functions.signature: omit<TObject extends object, TKey extends keyof TObject>(value: TObject, omitted: readonly TKey[]): Omit<TObject, TKey>

functions.name: pick
functions.purpose: A new object with only the listed keys the object has.
functions.signature: pick<TObject extends object, TKey extends keyof TObject>(value: TObject, picked: readonly TKey[]): Pick<TObject, TKey>

functions.name: sortBy
functions.purpose: A new array of the items sorted by each criterion in turn, the later ones breaking ties in the earlier, and stable, so items equal on every criterion keep their order: sortBy(bonds, ["sector", { by: "yield", order: "desc" }, (bond) => bond.issuer.name]) Missing values (null, undefined, NaN and invalid Dates) go last in either order. Strings compare through `Intl.Collator` with numeric ordering; Dates and Temporal values compare by value.
functions.signature: sortBy<TItem>(items: readonly TItem[], criteria: readonly SortCriterion<TItem>[]): TItem[]

functions.name: deepEqual
functions.purpose: Whether two values are deeply equal. Primitives compare as `===` does, except that NaN equals NaN. Arrays, Maps, Sets and plain objects compare by their contents, Dates by their time, and Temporal values by their own `equals`, or field by field for Durations. Two objects of different prototypes are never equal, any other object is equal only to itself, and symbol keys are not compared. Cycles are followed once.

functions.name: stableStringify
functions.purpose: JSON text with every object's keys in sorted order, so two equal values always write the same text. It writes what `JSON.stringify` writes in every other way: `toJSON` is called, undefined, functions and symbols are left out of objects and are `null` in arrays, and NaN and the infinities are `null`. Where `JSON.stringify` would write a Map or Set as `{}`, or have nothing to write at all, it throws `TypeError`, as it does for a bigint and a cycle.

functions.name: debounce
functions.purpose: Calls `func` once calls have stopped for `debounceMs`, with the last call's arguments: for a search box, or a layout saved as it is dragged. With the leading edge, the first call of a burst also runs at once.
functions.signature: debounce<TArgs extends unknown[]>(func: (...args: TArgs) => void, debounceMs: number, { edges = ["trailing"], signal }: TimingOptions = {}): DebouncedFunction<TArgs>

functions.name: rafThrottle
functions.purpose: Calls `func` at most once an animation frame, with the latest arguments: for pointer moves and scroll handlers that draw.
functions.signature: rafThrottle<TArgs extends unknown[]>(func: (...args: TArgs) => void): ControlledFunction<TArgs>

functions.name: sleep
functions.purpose: Resolves after `ms`, or rejects with the signal's reason, an `AbortError` unless it was given another, as soon as the signal aborts.

functions.name: throttle
functions.purpose: Calls `func` at most once every `throttleMs`: at once on the leading edge, and with the latest arguments at the end of the wait on the trailing edge, which then starts a new wait. Calls are never closer than `throttleMs`, where lodash's throttle can call again right after a trailing call.
functions.signature: throttle<TArgs extends unknown[]>(func: (...args: TArgs) => void, throttleMs: number, { edges = ["leading", "trailing"], signal }: TimingOptions = {}): ThrottledFunction<TArgs>

functions.name: assertNever
functions.purpose: For the `default` of a switch that handles every case: TypeScript fails the build when a case is added and not handled, and if a value the types ruled out still arrives at run time, this throws with it.

functions.name: invariant
functions.purpose: Throws `Error` with the message unless the condition holds, and narrows by it after: `invariant(row !== undefined, "The selected row is in the table.")`. The condition is a boolean, so that 0 and "" are never mistaken for false.
functions.signature: invariant(condition: boolean, message: string): asserts condition

functions.name: isPresent
functions.purpose: Whether a value is neither null nor undefined, for `filter(isPresent)` to narrow an array.

functions.name: downloadBlob
functions.purpose: Saves a Blob as a file named `name`, through a temporary link, as the browser's download does.

functions.name: toCsv
functions.purpose: CSV text: a header row of the columns' headers, then a record for each row. For Excel to read non-ASCII text, save it with a byte order mark: `new Blob(["\uFEFF", csv], { type: "text/csv" })`.
functions.signature: toCsv<TRow>(rows: readonly TRow[], columns: readonly Column<TRow>[]): string

functions.name: toTsv
functions.purpose: TSV text, which pastes into a spreadsheet's cells: the same as `toCsv`, separated by tabs.
functions.signature: toTsv<TRow>(rows: readonly TRow[], columns: readonly Column<TRow>[]): string

functions.name: parseCsv
functions.purpose: Reads CSV text into its records, leaving out blank ones, or says why it cannot: const reading = parseCsv(await file.text()); if (reading.ok) { const [header, ...rows] = reading.records; } else { show(reading.reason); // Line 7 opens a quoted field that never closes: ... } Fields are text, exactly as written; a record may hold more or fewer fields than another, which the caller checks against its header.

functions.name: readWorkbook
functions.purpose: Reads an Excel workbook's list of sheets, or says why the bytes are not a workbook it reads: const reading = await readWorkbook(await file.arrayBuffer()); if (reading.ok) { const [first] = reading.workbook.sheets.filter((sheet) => sheet.worksheet && !sheet.hidden); const rows = await reading.workbook.readSheet(first.name); } else { show(reading.reason); // It is protected with a password, or ... } A sheet's records are its rows as text, leaving out blank rows, each with the row's number in the sheet, as `parseCsv` gives a CSV's with their lines.
functions.signature: readWorkbook(bytes: ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array, { maxPartBytes = defaultMaxPartBytes }: WorkbookOptions = {}): Promise<WorkbookReading>

functions.name: addBusinessDays
functions.purpose: The business day `days` business days after `date`, or before it when `days` is negative: each step moves to the next business day in that direction, so the first step from a closed day lands on the nearest business day. Zero days leaves `date` as it is.
functions.signature: addBusinessDays(date: Temporal.PlainDate, days: number, options: CalendarOption = {}): Temporal.PlainDate

functions.name: businessDayOnOrAfter
functions.purpose: `date` if it is a business day, or else the first business day after it.

functions.name: businessDayOnOrBefore
functions.purpose: `date` if it is a business day, or else the last business day before it.

functions.name: businessDaysBetween
functions.purpose: The business days after `start` up to and including `end`, negative when `end` comes first. So `addBusinessDays(start, businessDaysBetween(start, end))` is `end` whenever `end` is a business day.
functions.signature: businessDaysBetween(start: Temporal.PlainDate, end: Temporal.PlainDate, options: CalendarOption = {}): number

functions.name: closingTime
functions.purpose: When the market closes on `date`, in its session's zone: the regular close, an early close, or `undefined` on a day it does not trade.

functions.purpose: One test for every route of `routeTree`: each renders the route in BasisApp, in a Node DOM, with its requests answered from the app's `fixtures/` as `vp dev`'s fixture mode answers them, then orval's generated handlers, and fails with an `ERROR` line, ending with its fix, for each request nothing answers, each error the page reports to telemetry, raises as a toast or writes to the console, a page that never finishes loading, and each rule of axe's it breaks. A route with a parameter, such as `/bonds/$security`, opens at the sample `params` gives it, or else at a fixture's value for it: one whose path it matches, as `GET /bonds/US91282CRF04` does, or whose operation takes a path parameter of the same name. Without `container` it checks the whole document, landmarks included, as after `renderApp`; with one, such as the `container` `render` returns, only what is inside it. It checks what needs no layout or stylesheet, in a Node DOM and in Chromium alike: names, labels, roles, ARIA, landmarks, headings, lists, tables, ids and focus. Colour contrast and the size of a target need the page drawn with its styles, and `vp run shot` checks them.

functions.purpose: The page's engine, from the nearest `ParallaxProvider`. Throws without one.

functions.name: useDataset
functions.purpose: Loads a table into the page's engine as `name`, from `source`, and reports the load's state. It loads again when `name`, `source` or the options change, so give it a stable source: bytes held in state or a query, or a function the React Compiler keeps. A null source waits, as `idle`. Views of the dataset, opened with `useView`, may open while it loads: they wait for its first rows. A first load shows as it arrives, from a source that streams: its views open on its first rows and see more each time the rows read have grown fourfold, while `progress` says how many have been read of how many are expected, and a grid's status bar how many are still to come. Sorts, filters and pivots apply to the rows so far and update as more arrive; a chart waits for the whole load, and an export is refused until it is done. A reload is read whole and checked before anything changes: its views keep the rows before it until it applies, and a refused reload leaves them so, while `progress` says how far it has read. When the engine runs out of memory it starts again empty and fails every view; a dataset that was loaded then loads its source again, and its views reopen. A dataset whose load was under way, most likely the one that ran the engine out of memory, fails with the reason until `reload` is called or the source changes, as does every dataset once the engine keeps stopping. Components that ask for the same name and the same source share one load, so a page whose cards and grid show one dataset fetches it once. When the last component that shows a dataset unmounts, the engine drops it and its memory goes to later loads; once the engine's memory, which never shrinks, has grown past what its tables need, it starts again with what is still shown, which loads again as after a restart.
functions.signature: useDataset<TRow extends AnyRow = AnyRow>(name: string, source: DatasetSource | null, options: LoadOptions = {}): Dataset<TRow>
functions.use: Once for each table a page shows, inside a ParallaxProvider; give the dataset to a Grid, a Pivot or a Chart.

functions.name: useView
functions.purpose: Opens a view of `dataset`, which `useDataset` loads, as `layout` describes it, and reports what the engine sends: its frames, its chart's reduction, its table's status, and why it failed. The layout's dataset is `dataset`'s. The view opens while its dataset loads, and waits for it. A changed layout updates the open view in place, and a changed viewport or chart window asks for that window, without reopening. When the engine restarts, the view fails with the reason, and opens again once the dataset has loaded again. With `onChart`, the chart's reductions go to it rather than into the state, and with `onFrame`, the frames do, so a scroll that asks `handle` for rows renders nothing.
functions.signature: useView<TRow extends AnyRow = AnyRow>(dataset: Dataset<TRow>, layout: LayoutFor<TRow>, options?: ViewOptions): View

functions.name: maxArrowBytes

Step 6.3.9 set it from the scale harness: 1,000,000 positions, 460 MB of Arrow and 40 columns, take 449 MB of WebAssembly and 1.3 GB of browser at their peak, and pivot in about 200 ms, 700 ms with the CPU held to 40 %. A narrow table holds more rows within it, and a wide one fewer.

functions.purpose: The most rows one table the app loads may have, far above what {@link maxArrowBytes} lets a table of a few columns hold: the grid's scrollbar lands on every row up to about 15,000,000. The engine counts them from the stream's batch headers before decoding any data.

modules.name: @basis/ui
modules.purpose: The components and their icons, the app shell, and the hooks and functions that go with them: what an app's pages import.

modules.name: @basis/ui/numbers
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/numbers`: display arithmetic on the doubles APIs send, so that no app adds a decimal library or rounds by hand. `sumPrecise` adds doubles exactly; the rest are tick rounding, Treasury prices in 32nds and the values a dashboard derives. Every number is a double and every rate a fraction; the number components round once, for display. Anything with a market convention, such as accrued interest, day counts, yields or risk, is the API's.

modules.name: @basis/ui/utils
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/utils`: only what modern JavaScript lacks, so that no app adds lodash. Each helper is modelled on es-toolkit's signature (MIT), so what agents know of lodash and es-toolkit carries over. The language already has the rest: `Object.groupBy` and `Map.groupBy`, `structuredClone`, `Array.prototype.toSorted`, `flat` and `at`, the Set methods, `Promise.withResolvers`, `AbortSignal.timeout`, and Temporal for dates.

modules.name: @basis/ui/dates
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/dates`: business days, periods, settlement, market status, tenors and staleness, on Temporal. Plain dates are `Temporal.PlainDate`; instants are shown in New York time. Every query takes a calendar, SIFMA's US bond market calendar unless it names the NYSE's or TARGET2's.

modules.name: @basis/ui/securities
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/securities`: CUSIP, ISIN and SEDOL checks, CUSIP to ISIN, branded identifier types, so a ticker cannot pass where a CUSIP is due, and a reader for text that may be any of the three.

modules.name: @basis/ui/testing
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/testing`: what an app's tests are written with, so one test runs both in Chromium and in a Node DOM, on a laptop with no browser (docs/design.md, Consumers). It is Testing Library's API, `renderApp` for the app at an address, `mockApi` for the API, `workbookFile` for an Excel workbook an import reads, `checkRoutes` for every route on the app's fixtures at once, and `expectAccessible` for axe's check of what a test rendered. A test that needs a real browser, for layout, focus or pixels, is named `*.browser.test.tsx` and may use Vitest's browser API instead; the preset's lint keeps that API out of every other test, and `basisTest({ browser: false })` runs every test but those.

modules.name: @basis/ui/fixtures
modules.purpose: `@basis/ui/fixtures`: fixture mode in the browser, and the fixture record format. `vp dev` starts it through the preset with no code in the app; a test builds its handlers with `fixtureHandlers` and `loadFixtureFiles`. It is an entry of its own so that MSW never reaches an app's build.

modules.name: @basis/ui/preset
modules.purpose: The Vite+ preset an app's vite.config.ts spreads in: its lint, its tasks, its plugins and its tests.

modules.name: @basis/parallax
modules.purpose: The grid, the pivot table and every chart, drawn on a canvas from a Rust engine in a Web Worker, with their React layer.

types.name: DatasetSource
types.purpose: Where a dataset's Arrow IPC stream comes from: bytes the app holds, or a function that fetches them. A function that returns the response itself, such as `() => fetch(url)`, streams it: its body moves to the engine as it arrives, and a first load's rows show batch by batch, the first long before the last has come. One that returns bytes, such as `() => fetch(url).then((response) => response.arrayBuffer())`, shows them once they have all come. Bytes the app holds are copied before they move to the engine, so the app's copy, such as a query cache's, stays readable; a function's bytes or body move without a copy, so it returns fresh ones each call. After the engine restarts, the hook loads the source again.

types.name: Rounding
types.purpose: How a value that falls between two representable results is rounded. - `half-away-from-zero`: to the nearest, a tie away from zero. Excel's `ROUND`, and the default here. - `half-even`: to the nearest, a tie to the even neighbour (banker's rounding, IEEE 754's default). - `toward-zero`: truncation. Python's `ROUND_DOWN`. - `away-from-zero`: any remainder rounds away from zero. Python's `ROUND_UP`. - `floor`: toward negative infinity. - `ceiling`: toward positive infinity.
